english.title: Breach sexual harm prevention order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, did something, namely **(..SPECIFY THING DONE..), that you were prohibited from doing by a sexual harm prevention order made by **(..SPECIFY COURT..) under section 343 of the Sentencing Act 2020, on **(..SPECIFY DATE ORDER WAS MADE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 354(1) and (4) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without reasonable excuse
did anything prohibited by a
SHPO

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) As per section 343, this offence relates to a breach of an SHPO made by the Court under section 345 of the Sentencing Act 2020.
(ii) For breaches of SHPOs made under sections 103A to 103K of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, see offence H11483 applying before 29th November 2022 and offence, H101094 applying from that date.
(iii) For the version of this offence in force from 29th November 2022, see offence H101093.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictable: maximum 5 years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
